# Statistics in SSR {.section}

## The stats half of SSR {.smaller}

Two halves running side by side: reasoning (arguments, rationality, critical thinking) and statistics. These are the statistics lectures.

- Block 1: getting back into statistics
    - NHST, correlation, regression
- Block 2: comparing means
    - t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square, non-parametric tests
- Block 3: multiple predictors
    - multiple regression, mediation, moderation

Each block closes with an interim exam.

## What will you learn? {.smaller}

Not just computing the right number. Three levels, and we want all three:

::: {.incremental}
- Statistical literacy: knowing the concepts and working the tools
    - Identify, describe, translate, interpret, read, compute
- Statistical reasoning: understanding *why* and *how* a method works
- Statistical thinking: using it in the wild
    - Apply: what method fits this situation?
    - Critique: reflect on the work of others
    - Evaluate: assign value to that work
    - Generalize: what does variation mean in the large scheme of life?
:::

Source: [ARTIST](http://web.archive.org/web/20221018074534/http://apps3.cehd.umn.edu/artist/glossary.html)

## Book {.smaller}

Field, *Discovering Statistics Using JASP*.

- Block 1: Chapters 1 through 8.8 (skipping Chapter 6)
- Companion website: [discoverjasp.com](https://discoverjasp.com/pages/exercises)
- You have the book, glossary included, during the exam

### Sections A to D {.smaller}

Every section carries a letter for difficulty, each rhyming with what it does to your brain:

- A is for brain *Attain*: everyone should get something out of these
- B is for brain *Bane*: more knowledge needed, at times a source of unhappiness
- C is for brain *Complain*: final-year or master's material
- D is for brain *Drain*: difficult enough to drain Field's own brain

We live mostly in A and B.

### Characters {.smaller}

Worth looking out for:

- Cramming Sam: key points of a chapter, summarized
- Smart Alex: end-of-chapter tasks, answers on the website
- Labcoat Leni: real data from real studies
- Oliver Twisted: extra material on the website
- Jane Superbrain: advanced tangents

## Software
- JASP
    - Download the latest version (0.98.1) from [the website](https://jasp-stats.org/download/)
    - Your main tool in SSR for handling data and conducting analyses
    - Also available in the virtual [UvA desktop](apps.uva.nl) and at any UvA computer
- R
    - Statistical programming language, under the hood of JASP and my SSR slides
    - Very optional, sometimes included in the slide for those interested
    - R ([language pack](https://www.r-project.org/)) and Rstudio ([coding environment](https://posit.co/downloads)) available on the exam computers

## Study tips {.smaller}

- Read the chapter *before* the lecture. The lecture is then your second pass, not your first
- Practice statistics in JASP yourself: WA, [Smart Alex tasks](https://discoverjasp.com/pages/smart_alex), and [Labcoat Leni examples](https://discoverjasp.com/pages/labcoat_leni)
- For a deeper dive, play with the [applets](https://johnnydoorn.github.io/teaching-statistics/ssr/overview-ssr.html#applets), consult the [JASP Video Library](https://jasp-stats.github.io/jasp-video-library/), ask questions on the Discussion Board or have a chat with Roenny
